sol.problem:
Nested oracle-call output writes are absent from writes, so they can change an outstanding invocation's ins without invalidating it. Reproduced a memoryless object containing normative inc8 and oracle @p (a:wire[8] in, b:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token), signature in=[8,8], tgt=8, fault=4, args=[token], regs { x:reg[8], out:reg[8], fr:reg[4], fr2:reg[4] }, body:
^entry():
x = lift.mov a
lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (x) out fr () ()
lift.oracle_call @inc8 tk (b) x fr2 () ()
lift.oracle_uncall @inc8 tk (x) out fr () ()
lift.retval out
After replacing stored hashes with hash output, check exits 0/status ok. run-oracle p --input 1,0 --budget 5 --arg token:3 returns {code:0,payload:3,steps:5}. Hand derivation: first call writes out=2; second changes x from 1 to 0 by XORing inc8(0)=1; the uncall XORs 1 rather than the original 2. The required outcome is load rejection under §5.5. The comment that oracle XOR deliveries commute is insufficient when a delivered location is another invocation's input.
sol.fix: Change src/call_discipline.rs::validate_matched_oracle_calls transfer to account for target and fault writes of BOTH lift.oracle_call and lift.oracle_uncall when invalidating other outstanding invocations. §5.5 requires "same token, callee, ins and mem values (no intervening row writes those locations or cells: suite F)"; §4.2 explicitly writes "tgt ^= payload; fr ^= code". Separate input/cell invalidation from any proven-commuting XOR-output exception so existing two-call/two-uncall cases remain legal; consume a matched inverse without accidentally invalidating its own identity. Add the exact witness to tests/r1_rules.rs, requiring Object::parse Err citing §5.5 and hash/check exit 1 with empty stdout. Also test clobber through the fault output and through another uncall. Positive: delete the middle call; B=4, token B=3, inputs 1,0 must give payload=0/code=0/steps=4 and complete prefix reversal.

sol.problem:
Permutation action calls do not transfer dependencies between mutable operands: reads contains ins and in-region cells but omits mut bundles and mut-region cells. Wrapping the now-rejected direct swap in a child call bypasses the fix. Reproduced memoryless child signature kind=perm_action, mut=[1,1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[], and parent signature kind=action, mut=[1,1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[]:
perm_action @child (a:wire mut, b:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
swap a b
action @a (t:wire mut, m:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
d = qalloc any 1
h d
action_call @child (d, m) () () ()
cx m t
adj action_call @child (d, m) () () ()
h d
qfree d
Rehashed check exits 0/status ok. run-action a --mut 0,0 exits 1 with §4.3 E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN and an exactly nonzero d=1 component of amplitude 0.5. Hand: H(d); SWAP(d,m); CX(m,t); SWAP(d,m) entangles d,t, and H(d) cannot release d. The same direct swap witness is now correctly rejected, so validation is not invariant under this elementary call wrapping.
sol.fix: Change src/validation.rs::validate_action_sequence call arm and Discipline call-effect bookkeeping. §6.1 says permutation action calls give "each mut: perm with S = mut ∪ ins ∪ cells(regions passed) ∪ Π" and "mut-region cells advance with the same S"; §6.2 binds cleanup to "its exact computing sequence" and §6.3 requires factorisation. Snapshot the OLD union of all mutable/interface operands and passed cells before updating any output, carry transitive dependencies to every output, and bind inverse cancellation jointly to the complete current call-output group and entry versions, analogous to the corrected exchange handling. Preserve non-permutation provenance/window effects. Add this exact witness to tests/r1_discipline.rs, requiring parse rejection citing §6.2, plus a mutable-region transfer variant. Positive: duplicate the middle cx m t; it already runs and reverses identically on all four t,m basis inputs and must remain accepted. Extend that positive to a superposed interface and add the child-call family to the differential generator.

sol.problem:
Repeated-squaring substitution treats opaque function applications as independent fixed ANF variables, even when their inputs change between iterations. Reproduced memoryless identity oracle signature in=[1], tgt=1, fault=4, args=[], body oracle @o (x:wire in) (t:wire) (f:wire[4]) () (); ^entry(): lift.retval x. Parent signature kind=perm_action, mut=[1,4], in=[], args=[token], mem=[], bounds=[2], body:
perm_action @a (t:wire mut, f:wire[4] mut) () () (tk:token) ()
regs {  } bounds {2}
^entry():
d = qborrow any 1
qloop 2 {
oracle_call @o tk (t) d f () ()
x t
}
qreturn d
Rehashed check exits 0/status ok without a certificate. run-action a --mut 0,0 --arg token:1 and --mut 1,0 both exit 1: §5.6 borrowed wires were not returned to their entry state. Hand: d_out=d_in XOR t XOR (t XOR 1)=d_in XOR 1; t is restored. Expanding the exact same loop into two straight-line call/x pairs correctly rejects at parse with §5.6. Thus Repeat changes the proof result for an identical circuit.
sol.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Evaluation::apply (Repeat composition and Opaque symbols) and the symbolic representation as needed. §4.6 says qloop executes "body n times"; §5.6 requires "operation ⊗ identity on every borrowed bundle" and "P_F = P′ ⊗ I_B". Compose opaque applications extensionally: substituting a loop-entry variable in an opaque input must substitute inside the application and re-identify it, rather than leaving the old symbol constant. An alternative sound proof path is to prove every opaque input invariant across iterations and otherwise require the verified §12 borrow_frames certificate route; never claim factorisation from the present frozen-symbol substitution. Add the exact loop and its unrolled equivalent to tests/r1_borrow.rs, both requiring §5.6 rejection without a claim. Positive: remove x t from the body; both calls then have the same input and must parse and preserve every borrowed bit for token B=1, every t,f,d, with forward/adjoint restoration. This positive was reproduced through reverse for t,f=(0,0) and (1,15). Add changing-input opaque loops to the differential generator.

sol.problem:
The classical normalized-call arm discards call.control for typing, allowing a non-wire ctl operand to pass load validation and then hard-error at execution. Reproduced a memoryless action @a (t:wire mut) () () () (), signature mut=[1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[], body ^entry(): x t; and CC signature params=[i8,qreg[1]], results=[], body:
fn cc @p (c:i8, q:qreg[1]) () () () ()
^entry():
ctl c action_call @a (q) () () ()
ret
After rehash, hash and check both exit 0/status ok. run-cc p --arg 1 --arg qreg:0 exits 1 with §3.3 region operand is not a qreg, with no result JSON. An unknown control similarly escapes this arm's rd checks. By comparison, changing c to qreg[1] and its signature accordingly yields a successful two-step COMPLETED run. Additional reproduced variants: unknown ctl name is accepted then gives a one-step FAULT_UB_TRAP result; qreg[2] control is accepted then hard-errors ctl requires qreg[1]; using the target q itself as a qreg[1] control is accepted then hard-errors effective control aliases target.
sol.fix: In src/validation.rs::classical_instruction, after normalize_call and before validate_region_call, resolve any control using rd (so forward type inference still works) and require Type::Qreg(1). §4.7 defines "ctl w <call> ≡ the call under qpred w"; §3.3 binds a qreg[n] to a wire[n] slot "bit for bit" and §4.8 requires fixed "operand kinds and a result type". Therefore an i8, token, unknown name or qreg[2] cannot fill the single-wire control slot and must be rejected at load, citing §3.3/§4.8. Add the exact witness and these variants to tests/parser.rs/tests/cli_xam.rs, expecting parse Err and hash/check exit 1 with empty stdout. Keep a distinct qreg[1] control/target positive, with control values 0 and 1, exact controlled-X results and full reversal. Also apply the §3.3 effective-control/target disjointness check to normalized CC calls instead of relying on a later simulator error.

sol.problem:
Borrow analysis omits the effective controls from Node::Other for a non-permutation action call. Reproduced a memoryless object with both signatures kind=action, mut=[1], in=[], mem=[], args=[], bounds=[]:
action @child (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
h t
action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
d = qborrow any 1
ctl d action_call @child (t) () () ()
qreturn d
Rehashed check exits 0/status ok, without a borrow certificate. run-action a --mut 0 exits 0 with state {"0":[1,0]} because its default borrow pool is |0>; that single pool value masks the invalid borrow use. Hand: on borrowed |0>, the target is unchanged; on borrowed |1>, it receives H, so the full map is |0><0|_d tensor I_t + |1><1|_d tensor H_t, not U_t tensor I_d. A borrowed superposition and t=0 become (|0>_d|0>_t + |1>_d|+>_t)/sqrt(2), correlating d and t. Replacing the call with qpred d; h t; qunpred d correctly makes hash reject with §5.6: borrowed wire touched by a non-permutation instruction. The call compiler records only actual mut/in bundles in Other(t), losing d.
sol.fix: Change src/borrow.rs::Compiler::compile in the fallback non-permutation action-call arm: Node::Other must include every wire the call touches, including its effective predicate controls and normalized ctl control, as well as interface bundles and passed region cells. §5.6 says borrowed wires are "touched (as control or target) only inside borrow frames", which are "permutation-only subcircuits", and requires "operation ⊗ identity on every borrowed bundle". §4.7 makes ctl exactly the call under qpred. The exact witness must reject at load citing §5.6, just as the direct controlled-H form already does. Add both forms to tests/r1_borrow.rs, plus an inherited qpred d around the call, requiring parse Err and CLI hash/check exit 1. Positive: use a perm_action child containing x t and invoke it twice under d; that complete permutation frame is identity on t and d and must remain accepted, with exact forward/adjoint execution for both borrowed entry bits and a superposed borrowed input.

codex.problem:
Oracle calls have implicit writes to tgt/fr, but transfer constructs writes only from row.lhs and lift.perm_call mutable operands. Its assumption that all oracle XOR deliveries commute misses a delivery into another outstanding invocation's input. Reproduced a memoryless object (ptr_width=32), oracle i with in=[8],tgt=8,fault=4,args=[], and oracle o with in=[],tgt=8,fault=4,args=[token]. Bodies:
oracle @i (x:wire[8] in) (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () ()
^entry():
lift.retval x
oracle @o () (t:wire[8]) (f:wire[4]) () (tk:token)
regs { a:reg[8], b:reg[8], r:reg[8], fr:reg[4], fr2:reg[4] }
^entry():
a = lift.const.i8 1
b = lift.const.i8 2
lift.oracle_call @i tk (a) r fr () ()
lift.oracle_call @i tk (b) a fr2 () ()
lift.oracle_uncall @i tk (a) r fr () ()
lift.retval r
After rehashing, check exits 0/status ok; run-oracle /dev/stdin o --input "" --budget 6 --arg token:1,0,0,0 returns {code:0,payload:2,steps:6}; step-check --exhaustive with those options also returns ok (one case). Hand trace: first r=1, intervening call changes a=1 XOR 2=3, then uncall changes r=1 XOR 3=2. The required unchanged input is violated, so the object must never reach execution.
codex.fix: Change src/call_discipline.rs::validate_matched_oracle_calls transfer to include implicit target and fault writes of both lift.oracle_call and lift.oracle_uncall when invalidating other outstanding invocations whose ins intersect those locations. Clear address-constant knowledge for those destinations too. Preserve the legitimate commuting shared-output/multiplicity cases: distinguish writes to an outstanding input from XOR updates to its target/fault. §5.5 requires "same token, callee, ins and mem values (no intervening row writes those locations or cells: suite F)"; §4.2 explicitly writes "tgt ^= payload; fr ^= code". Expected: the exact object above is rejected at parse/check with §5.5 (CLI exit 1, empty stdout). Add it to tests/r1_rules.rs and a variant where another invocation's fault destination writes a tracked input. Positive: remove the middle call, use outer B=5 and token B=1; require payload=0,code=0,steps=5 and complete prefix reversal. Keep two-call/two-uncall positives.

codex.section: §6.1–§6.3, §5.1; src/validation.rs::Object::validate_action_sequence region-call arm and Discipline dependency bookkeeping
codex.problem:
The exchange fix can be bypassed by putting the exchange inside a permutation action. Region-call transfer reads only ins and in-regions, omitting mutable bundles and mutable regions; it updates outputs separately. Reproduced memoryless signatures: c kind=perm_action,mut=[1,1],in=[],mem=[],args=[],bounds=[]; a kind=action with the same widths. Bodies:
perm_action @c (a:wire mut, b:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
swap a b
action @a (t:wire mut, m:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
d = qalloc any 1
h d
action_call @c (d, m) () () ()
cx m t
adj action_call @c (d, m) () () ()
h d
qfree d
Rehashed check exits 0/status ok. run-action /dev/stdin a --mut 0,0 exits 1 with §4.3 E_QREG_NOT_CLEAN, an exactly nonzero [false,false,true] component of amplitude 0.5. Hand trace: H(d), SWAP(d,m), CX(m,t), SWAP(d,m) entangles d with t; final H(d) does not clean d. Replacing child swap with cx a b yields the same accepted dirty-release failure. Doubling the middle cx m t is accepted and executes as identity, state {"00":[1,0]}. Direct versions of this class now reject, so validation depends unsoundly on a call boundary.
codex.fix: Change src/validation.rs::validate_action_sequence's action_call/adj/ctl transfer and Discipline to snapshot all old mut, ins and region-cell dependencies before changing any output, propagate their union to every mut bundle/cell, and retain transitive readers of those values across a call and its adjoint. Joint inverses must bind entry versions and cancel all participating outputs consistently, as the exchange fix already does. §6.1 specifies "each mut: perm with S = mut ∪ ins ∪ cells(regions passed) ∪ Π" and the same S for mut-region cells; §6.2 binds cleanup to its "exact computing sequence"; §6.3 requires factorisation from remaining state. Expected: both quoted swap-child and CX-child negatives reject at load citing §6.2. Add them to tests/r1_discipline.rs, together with a mut-region transfer analogue. Positive controls doubling the middle CX must parse and execute forward/adjoint on all t,m basis entries and a superposed entry, returning clean workspace and exact entry state after reversal. Extend tests/r1_fuzz_discipline.rs with equivalent direct versus called computations.

codex.problem:
The borrow compiler hoists child-local regions as Alloc nodes, never appends their function-exit restoration/release, then reverses that incomplete node sequence for an adjoint call. Node::adjoint turns Alloc into Free, so an adjoint-only invocation tries to free a symbolic region that was never allocated. Reproduced a memoryless object, both functions kind=perm_action with mut=[1],in=[],mem=[],args=[],bounds=[]:
perm_action @c (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
qregion r 1 1
x t
x t
perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()
^entry():
b = qborrow any 1
cx b t
adj action_call @c (t) () () ()
cx b t
qreturn b
The hash CLI exits 1: "§5.6: a wire released inside a borrow frame is not clean". Removing only "adj " makes hash exit 0. Hand derivation: c allocates a zero region, performs X twice, restores/releases that unchanged region, so c=c†=I; parent is CX(b,t) I CX(b,t)=I on every t,b, including b entangled with an external system. This is a false rejection of a defined valid program, not an uncertifiable black-box borrow operation.
codex.fix: In src/borrow.rs compile complete local-region lifetimes for inlined functions: unconditional allocation and image preparation at entry, body in the selected direction, inverse image gates and release at exit. Either reverse the complete entry/body/exit node sequence or keep the lifetime wrapper fixed and reverse only the body; do not reverse a lone Alloc into an unmatched Free. Represent image preparation separately or make lifecycle nodes preserve the image on adjoint, since Node::adjoint currently discards it. §4.6 says "created at function entry" and "back at its image before exit, image gates reversed, cells released clean"; §5.3 includes "qregion creation ↔ release". Expected: the exact object parses; run-action a --mut 0/1 and reverse succeed with the same t and equals_entry=true. Add a tests/r1_borrow.rs regression requiring acceptance and forward/adjoint/exact restoration for every t,b basis value and a borrowed system entangled with a reference. Also cover a nonzero image (e.g. qregion r 1 4 @image, one-byte image ff) and a declaration nested in a zero-trip loop; these must have the same function-entry lifetime in forward and adjoint calls.
